_readme: Regulatory limits used to define a CONFIRMED VIOLATION. Values are in the dataset's own units (mg/L unless noted). 'limit' is the STRICTER of the EPA and WHO values when both exist. 'basis' is 'health' (enforceable / health-based) or 'aesthetic' (taste, odour, staining - not a health violation). A null limit means no federal/WHO numeric limit, so that chemical is never counted. Filled in from general knowledge: please double-check each number against the current EPA (Drinking Water Regulations) and WHO (Guidelines for Drinking-water Quality) pages before you present.

aluminium.note: EPA secondary (SMCL) 0.05-0.2; WHO has no health-based value

ammonia.note: WHO taste/odour threshold; no health-based value

barium.note: stricter of EPA MCL 2.0 and WHO 1.3

cadmium.note: stricter of EPA MCL 0.005 and WHO 0.003

bacteria.note: coliform/E. coli must be absent; dataset values are 0-1 (units unknown)

viruses.note: target is zero; dataset values are 0-1 (units unknown)

nitrates.note: EPA 10 as nitrogen; WHO 50 as nitrate

nitrites.note: EPA 1 as nitrogen; WHO 3 as nitrite

perchlorate.note: no federal MCL and no WHO guideline in my notes; verify current status; not counted

uranium.note: EPA MCL and WHO provisional guideline
